main_text.l: IOANNI ARISKINO
comiti Marriæ, Scotorum
proregi.
SI quis Ariskinum memoret per bella ferocem,
Pace grauem nulli, tempore vtroque pium,
Si quis opes sine fastu, animum sine fraude carente,
Rebus in ambiguis suspicione fidem,
Si, quod ob has dotes suis iactata procellis
Fugit in illius patria fessa sinum,
Vera quidem memoret, sed non & propria: laudes
Qui pariter petet has vnus & alter erit.
Illud ei proprium est, longo quod in ordine vitæ
Nil odium, aut liuor quod reprehendat habet.
MATTHÆO STVARTO, Leuinię Comiti Scotorum Proregi.
REgis auus, regis pater, alto e sanguine Regum,
Imperio quorum terra Britanna subesit,
Matthæus genuit Leuinia: Gallia fuit:
Pulso Anglus thalamum remque decusque dedit.
Capi inuicta manu: famam virtute refelli:
Arma armis vici, consilióque dolos.
Gratus in ingratos, patriam iusteque pieque
Cum regerem hostili perfidia cecidi.

page.notes: Long s in the printed text is a plain s; the poem line "Pulso Anglus thalamum remque decusque dedit" is copied as printed and may be doubtful. Several words in the second poem are doubtful and marked with [?]: "Capi" and "Gratus" are as printed in the scan, the first poem's "Si, quod" is read with a comma. Greek-free page. Heads are italic or spaced capitals in the scan; the poem lines are italic and printed as separate lines, which I have run together into stanza paragraphs.
